quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following protects a rider the best?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face if you crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Riding next to another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Lets you talk to the other rider.
Makes it easier for other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcycle. It limits both riders' escape routes if danger appears.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes involve:

options.text: Riders who have ridden their motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders who have ridden their motorcycle for less than six months.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on their bike.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Works as well as a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not provide the same protection as goggles or a face shield. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn:

options.text: Should be used all the time.
Should be used if you think another driver may move into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used if you think another driver may move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Use your signals, lights, position, and horn to tell other drivers where you are. Use your horn when you need to alert someone quickly, like when another driver is moving into your lane unsafely.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: To reduce injury in a crash, wear all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing to reduce injury. A windshield does not help prevent injury.

questions.question: To lean the motorcycle for a turn, you should:

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Push the handgrip in the direction you want to go to make the motorcycle lean and turn.

questions.question: When a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left, it means the rider:
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals to show turns or stops instead of turn signals. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes left.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: There are few vehicles on the road.
Drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Increase your following distance in these situations.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by closing the throttle and using the brakes if needed.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Throttle down and use the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time with firm pressure. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When a group of riders is passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, the riders should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: When a group is passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. Wait until the rider ahead finishes passing before you start.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: When selecting a helmet, make sure it is all of the following, except:

options.text: Designed to meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at a motorcycle but fail to notice it.

questions.question: When you have mounted your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes all work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: To be effective, an eye or face shield should be all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Eye protection must be free of scratches, resist penetration, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. It should also provide clear side views and fit over eyeglasses. It does not need to be airtight.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: While a staggered formation is usually recommended, switch to single-file when riding through curves, turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
Provide a good view of the shoulder.
Provide a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen by them. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help others see you and keep you out of their blind spots. It should help you avoid hazards, protect your lane, show other drivers what you plan to do, help you avoid wind blasts from trucks, and give you a way to escape danger.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in their blind spot, and they might block your escape route if danger appears. If you are riding next to another vehicle, either go faster or drop back.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Help other drivers see you more easily.
Don't improve how visible you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you more easily.
questions.explanation: Choose a brightly-colored helmet. The helmet will protect you in a crash. The bright color will also help other drivers on the road see you.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have used that motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Travel to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: The right lane position protects your space and shows other drivers your intentions.
